definitions.explanation: Indicates that something happens prior to another event or time.
Indicates a position in front of something.

examples.japanese: {寝|ね}る{前|まえ}に{歯|は}を{磨|みが}きます。
examples.english: I brush my teeth before going to bed.
examples.notes: Time: verb dictionary form + 前に

examples.japanese: {出|で}かける{前|まえ}に{電気|でんき}を{消|け}してください。
examples.english: Please turn off the lights before going out.

examples.japanese: {食事|しょくじ}の{前|まえ}に{手|て}を{洗|あら}ってください。
examples.english: Please wash your hands before the meal.

examples.japanese: {会議|かいぎ}の{前|まえ}に{資料|しりょう}を{準備|じゅんび}しておきます。
examples.english: I'll prepare the materials before the meeting.

examples.japanese: {雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}る{前|まえ}に{帰|かえ}りましょう。
examples.english: Let's go home before it rains.

examples.japanese: {駅|えき}の{前|まえ}に{会|あ}いましょう。
examples.english: Let's meet in front of the station.

examples.japanese: {学校|がっこう}の{前|まえ}にバス{停|てい}があります。
examples.english: There's a bus stop in front of the school.

examples.japanese: {私|わたし}の{前|まえ}に{座|すわ}ってください。
examples.english: Please sit in front of me.

examples.japanese: コンビニは{銀行|ぎんこう}の{前|まえ}にあります。
examples.english: The convenience store is in front of the bank.

examples.japanese: {家|いえ}の{前|まえ}に{大|おお}きな{木|き}が{立|た}っています。
examples.english: A large tree stands in front of the house.

notes: {前|まえ}に has two main uses. For time, use [verb dictionary form] + {前|まえ}に or [noun] + の{前|まえ}に to mean 'before doing something.' For location, use [noun] + の{前|まえ}に to mean 'in front of.' The opposite for time is {後|あと}で (after).
